# Court-Grade Evidence Substrate (E1 — Trust Core)

This document maps each technical control to the evidentiary requirement it
satisfies. It is written to be attachable to an expert affidavit supporting
authentication under **FRE 901(b)(9)** (process or system producing an
accurate result) and to support a self-authentication posture under
**FRE 902(13)/(14)** (certified records generated by an electronic process /
data copied from an electronic device, as authenticated by a process of
digital identification).

> Honest scope note: software produces *evidence artifacts and a verifiable
> process*. Admissibility is a legal determination made by a court; this
> substrate exists so that a qualified expert can truthfully testify that
> the system reliably produces accurate, tamper-evident records.

## Control → requirement map

| Control | Implementation | Evidentiary function |
|---|---|---|
| Signed hash chain (`.zarc`) | `kernel/provenance.py` — every line Ed25519-signed, SHA-256 `prev_hash` linkage, genesis `"0"*64` | **Integrity**: any alteration of any record breaks the chain detectably (`verify_chain`). |
| Canonical serialization | `shared/canonical.py` — sorted keys, no whitespace, non-finite floats rejected, single home enforced by arch test | **Reliability of process**: byte-identical records across time, machines, and operators. |
| Deterministic replay | `application/semantics_replay_interpreter.py`, ADR-004 — timestamps derived from command fields, no wall-clock in Plane 1 | **Accuracy**: the computation that produced a record can be re-executed and byte-compared by an independent party. |
| **Trusted timestamping (RFC 3161)** | `infrastructure/tsa_verifier.py` + `services/anchor_orchestrator/timestamp_client.py` — messageImprint match, nonce echo, CMS signature, **pinned trust chain** (`config/tsa_trust/`), `id-kp-timeStamping` EKU | **Trusted time**: records existed *no later than* an independently issued, cryptographically verified timestamp. Forged or unverifiable tokens raise `TsaForgeryError` and trigger the freeze controller — they are never silently used. |
| **Chain of custody** | `domain/custody.py` + `application/custody_log.py` — acquire/transfer/examine/seal/export/verify events as `.zarc` entries, continuity validated fail-closed | **Custody (FRE 901(a))**: every handling of evidence is attributed (actor, role), content-bound (`evidence_hash`), and ordered; gaps or impossible transfers are refuted at write time. |
| **Witness cosigned checkpoints** | `domain/witness_checkpoint.py` + `application/witness_service.py` — Merkle commitment over chain entries, origin signature (HSM-capable), k-of-n independent witness cosignatures | **Corroboration / non-repudiation**: independent parties vouch for the chain state; per-entry inclusion proofs let an auditor confirm one record against a cosigned root without exposing the rest of the chain. |
| HSM key custody | `infrastructure/pkcs11_signing_backend.py` — signing keys resident in PKCS#11 token, never in process memory | **Key custody**: the entity controlling the HSM controls the signatures; key compromise of the application host does not compromise signing capability. |
| Fail-closed governance | QC gate, `CBI0BlockedError`, `FreezeController.fork_detected` | **Process discipline**: on any integrity anomaly the system halts and records the anomaly — there is no silent-degradation path. |

## Known limitations (disclosed for the evidence file)

1. **No revocation checking** — TSA trust is pinned-anchor offline
   validation; no CRL/OCSP in this phase. Compromise response is anchor
   removal + freeze + re-anchor (see `config/tsa_trust/README.md`).
2. **Local tier-1 timestamps are self-asserted** — when the TSA is
   unreachable, locally signed tokens are used and are marked
   `verified=False`. Only tier-2 tokens with a passing
   `TsaVerificationReport` count as trusted time.
3. **Append-only is conventional, not WORM-enforced** — hash chaining
   makes tampering *detectable*; storage-level write prevention (fsync
   policy, permissions, DB REVOKEs) is phase E2.
4. **Verification reports are not yet signed artifacts** — machine-signed
   verification certificates are phase E2 alongside sealed packages.

## Auditor quickstart

```bash
# Verify chain integrity (signatures + linkage)
python -c "from egregore.kernel.provenance import Provenance; \
import sys; sys.exit(0 if Provenance('chain.zarc', signing_key_hex='00'*32).verify_chain() else 1)"

# Verify a block chain end-to-end (linkage, merkle, integrity, signatures)
python scripts/verify_block_chain.py <blocks.zarc> --pubkey <verify-key-hex>

# Custody lifecycle for one evidence item
#   -> CustodyLog(provenance).history("EV-001")

# Prove one entry against a cosigned checkpoint
#   -> WitnessService.prove_entry(i) + verify_entry_inclusion(proof, checkpoint)
```

## Phase E2 (not in this increment)

BagIt-style sealed evidence packages (manifest + fixity + tag files),
WORM storage enforcement, signed machine-readable verification reports,
and the public verification API (replacing the current stub endpoint).
